newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong Democrats pay tribute to China's Deng.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong Democrats pay tribute to China's Deng.

text.p: Two leaders of Hong Kong's Democratic Party, who have been vocal critics of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping, on Friday paid their respects to mark the patriarch's death.
Democratic Party vice-chairmen Yeung Sum and Anthony Cheung paid their respects at a shrine set up at the headquarters of the Xinhua News Agency, China's de facto diplomatic mission in Hong Kong.
Yeung denied the party was trying to mend fences with the Chinese authorities.
"No. We still talk about the disgrace of Mr Deng which very few people dare to speak about at this time," Yeung told reporters after tendering his condolences.
"We also ask the present leaders to restate their position on June 4," he said.

The Democratic Party, Hong Kong's largest, was born out the shock that gripped the British colony in the aftermath of the brutal crackdown on pro-democracy demonstrations around Beijing's Tiananmen Square in June 4, 1989.
Deng, who ordered the crackdown, died on Wednesday at the age of 92 of lung problems and complications from Parkinson's disease.
Long lines of mourners formed outside the Xinhua building in Hong Kong on Thursday and Friday.
Colonial Governor Chris Patten and his designated successor, Tung Chee-hwa, paid their tributes on Thursday.

The Democratic Party was branded by Beijing as "subversive" and pointedly excluded from committees shaping the future the territory when China resumes control of Hong Kong from Britain at midnight on June 30 this year.
